> Written for blit386 1.8.1, which is not on npm yet. The newest release is 1.8.0, so an API on this page may be missing from the version npm installs until 1.8.1 ships.

Live version: https://demos.blit386.dev/gamepad-input. This is the demo-site source, not a standalone file: it imports and calls helpers from `./shared/` (themed panels, on-screen D-pad, post-process fallbacks), which are not part of blit386 and are not on npm. To run it as is, keep those files from https://github.com/blit386/blit386/tree/main/packages/demos/src/shared at the same relative path. To adapt it, remove or replace the helper imports and every call to them.

```js title="gamepad-input.js"
/*

Gamepad Input: analog sticks, triggers, and face-button masks.
@description A tiny hover-pod playground for gamepads: connect status, analog sticks, triggers, and button masks.
@ogScale integer

Part of the BLIT386 demo series.

Prerequisites:
  - Basics: https://demos.blit386.dev/basics
  - Keyboard Input: https://demos.blit386.dev/keyboard-input

Live version: https://demos.blit386.dev/gamepad-input

Guides:
  - Input: https://blit386.dev/docs/guides/input#keyboard
  - Input: https://blit386.dev/docs/guides/input#frame-timing-semantics
  - Game Loop: https://blit386.dev/docs/guides/game-loop#smoothing-motion-between-updates
  - Overlay: https://blit386.dev/docs/guides/overlay#optional-bands

Reference:
  - Game Loop: https://blit386.dev/docs/api/game-loop#interpolating-render-state-with-renderalpha
  - Overlay: https://blit386.dev/docs/api/overlay#event-tags

---

WHAT YOU WILL SEE
-----------------

A title strip across the top and two columns under it, both ending on the same line.

On the left, a "Controls" panel lists what each stick, trigger, and button does. Below it,
a dark arena with a border fills the rest of the column: inside it a small square "hover
pod" with a white outline and a small crosshair. Until a gamepad is connected, a warm
prompt sits near the top of the arena (on a touch screen it says "This demo needs a
gamepad" instead).

On the right, a status panel from the shared UI kit, titled with how many gamepads the
browser reports ("Gamepads: 0"): a pip for player one's connection, pips for A, B, the
(A|B) mask, any button, L2 and R2, then the raw left and right stick numbers (LX, LY, RX,
RY) and a "Throttle" meter that fills with trigger pressure. Under it, a "Pod" panel
shows the pod's current color, whether the trail is on, and a "Boost" meter that empties
as an R2 boost runs out. When the gamepad connects, a "Gamepad connected" tag lands on the
engine overlay's timing chart.

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
-------------------

- BT.isGamepadConnected(player) and BT.gamepadCount for connection status, with a simple
  rising-edge check to react once when a pad appears.
- BT.getAxis(axis, player) with BT.AXIS_LEFT_X / AXIS_LEFT_Y / AXIS_RIGHT_X / AXIS_RIGHT_Y
  (-1 to +1) and BT.AXIS_TRIGGER_L / AXIS_TRIGGER_R (0 to 1), dead-zone filtered by the
  engine.
- Button masks: BT.isDown(BT.BTN_A | BT.BTN_B, player) is true when either button is
  held.
- The triggers as digital buttons: BT.isDown(BT.BTN_L2, player) and
  BT.isPressed(BT.BTN_R2, player) turn on at half pull.
- BT.isAnyButtonDown(player) for "is anything held" checks.
- Smoothing motion with BT.renderAlpha and Vector2i.lerp between the previous and current
  tick positions.
- BT.PLAYER_ONE as the player index, and BT.assignTag for the timing chart.

HOW THE POD IS STEERED
----------------------

- The left stick moves the pod around the arena; the right stick moves the crosshair.
- Trigger pressure grows the pod from 10 up to 20 pixels (a little "throttle" feeling).
  Whichever trigger reads higher wins.
- A cycles the pod through three colors, B toggles a breadcrumb trail, Start recenters
  the pod and crosshair.
- R2, read as a button, gives the pod a 20-tick speed boost at double speed.

Face buttons for player 0 merge keyboard and gamepad, so the default keyboard map also
works for A (Space or B), B (N), and Start (5). The sticks, triggers, L2, and R2 are
gamepad only.

TRY THIS
--------

- Plug in a gamepad and press any button so the browser wakes it up.
- Move the left stick to fly the pod; move the right stick to drag the crosshair. The
  default dead zone is large, so push the stick most of the way before anything moves.
- Squeeze either trigger and watch the pod grow and the Throttle meter fill.
- Hold A and B together and watch the "(A|B) mask" pip in the panel light up.
- Pull R2 past half way while moving the left stick to feel the boost; the "R2 held" pip
  lights once R2 passes half pull.
- Press B to turn the trail on, fly around, and press B again to clear it.
- Press the backquote key (`) to open the engine overlay and look for the "Gamepad
  connected" tag on the timing chart.

*/

import { bootstrap, BT, Color32, Rect2i, Vector2i } from 'blit386';

import { applyTheme, ui, UI_ANCHORS } from './shared/ui.js';

/** @typedef {import('blit386').Palette} Palette */

// Screen size in display pixels. 288 is tall enough for every row of the status panel.
const DISPLAY_W = 320;
const DISPLAY_H = 288;

// Every gamepad read in this demo is for the first player slot (index 0).
const PLAYER = BT.PLAYER_ONE;

// Scene palette indices. Slot 0 stays transparent; toy colors start at 1. The shared UI
// kit's applyTheme() adds its own twelve colors way up at slots 240+, so nothing
// collides.
const C_POD_OUTLINE = 1; // pod outline white; doubles as the timing-chart render bar
const C_ARENA = 2; // filled interior of the steering arena
const C_ARENA_BORDER = 3; // arena border rectangle
const C_CHART_DIM = 4; // timing-chart update bar (soft gray)
const C_CHART_TAG = 5; // timing-chart milestone tag color (amber)
const C_POD_A = 6; // first pod color (cycles with A)
const C_POD_B = 7; // second pod color
const C_POD_C = 8; // third pod color
const C_TRAIL = 9; // white with a lower alpha value, for the trail pixels
const C_AIM = 10; // right-stick crosshair color

// Layout on a 4-pixel grid: 4 pixels from the screen edges, 4 between panels. Two
// columns under the 22-pixel title strip, 204 and 104 pixels wide
// (4 + 204 + 4 + 104 + 4 = 320).
//
//   - Right column: the Gamepad panel (22 title + 7 pip rows + 4 axis rows + a 23-pixel
//     meter + 11 bottom = 166 pixels), then the Pod panel (22 + 2 rows + a meter + 11 =
//     76 pixels). Both columns end at y = 272, above the bottom-left 17x13 pixels the
//     engine overlay keeps for its toggle hint.
//   - Left column: the Controls panel (22 + 4 rows + 11 = 73 pixels), then the arena,
//     which stretches down to the same bottom line as the right column.
const EDGE = 4;
const GAP = 4;
const TOP_Y = 26;
const LEFT_W = 204;
const RIGHT_W = 104;
const RIGHT_X = DISPLAY_W - EDGE - RIGHT_W;
const GAMEPAD_PANEL_H = 22 + 7 * 10 + 4 * 10 + 23 + 11;
const POD_PANEL_Y = TOP_Y + GAMEPAD_PANEL_H + GAP;
const POD_PANEL_H = 22 + 2 * 10 + 23 + 11;
const COLUMN_BOTTOM = POD_PANEL_Y + POD_PANEL_H;
const CONTROLS_PANEL_H = 22 + 4 * 10 + 11;

// Meters in the right column fill the panel's content width (the panel minus 9 pixels of
// padding on each side).
const METER_W = RIGHT_W - 18;

// The play arena rectangle, in display pixels: under the Controls panel, down to the
// bottom of the right column.
const ARENA_X = EDGE;
const ARENA_Y = TOP_Y + CONTROLS_PANEL_H + GAP;
const ARENA_W = LEFT_W;
const ARENA_H = COLUMN_BOTTOM - ARENA_Y;

// Names of the three pod colors, in the same order A cycles through them.
const POD_COLOR_NAMES = ['green', 'red', 'blue'];

// Pod size in pixels: 10 at rest, up to 10 more at full trigger pull. POD_SPEED is how
// many pixels per tick a fully pushed stick moves it.
const POD_BASE_SIZE = 10;
const POD_MAX_EXTRA_SIZE = 10;
const POD_SPEED = 3;

// An R2 press gives the pod a short speed burst: BOOST_TICKS update ticks at BOOST_FACTOR
// times the normal speed.
const BOOST_TICKS = 20;
const BOOST_FACTOR = 2;

// Pixels per tick for the right-stick crosshair, and how many trail points we keep.
const AIM_SPEED = 4;
const TRAIL_MAX = 28;

// Formats a stick axis value (-1 to +1) as a fixed-width string like '+0.50' or '-0.32'.
// Writing the '+' out keeps every row the same width, so the numbers in the panel do not
// jiggle left and right as the sign flips.
function formatAxis(value) {
    // toFixed(2) rounds to two decimal places and always prints both (0.5 -> '0.50').
    return (value >= 0 ? '+' : '') + value.toFixed(2);
}

// Tiny gamepad playground that visualizes sticks, triggers, and buttons.
class Demo {
    /** @type {Palette | null} */
    palette = null;

    // Palette slots of the shared UI theme colors, filled by applyTheme() in init().
    /** @type {ReturnType<typeof applyTheme> | null} */
    theme = null;

    // Pod position in integer display pixels.
    podPos = new Vector2i(Math.floor(DISPLAY_W / 2), Math.floor(DISPLAY_H / 2));

    // Small cursor moved by the right stick so both sticks have visible jobs.
    aimPos = new Vector2i(Math.floor(DISPLAY_W / 2) + 28, Math.floor(DISPLAY_H / 2));

    // Pod and aim position at the START of the most recent update() tick, before this
    // tick's stick input moved them. render() blends between these and podPos/aimPos
    // using BT.renderAlpha so the pod and aim cursor glide smoothly between ticks instead
    // of jumping - see the Game Loop guide linked in the header. Start equal to
    // podPos/aimPos so the very first frame does not blend in from a stale position.
    prevPodPos = this.podPos;

    prevAimPos = this.aimPos;

    // Trail points for the optional motion history, newest last.
    /** @type {Vector2i[]} */
    trail = [];

    // Whether B has switched the trail on.
    trailEnabled = false;

    // Cycles through three pod colors when A is pressed: 0, 1, 2, then back to 0.
    podColorIndex = 0;

    // Update ticks of boost left. R2 (the right trigger as a DIGITAL button) starts it.
    boostTicks = 0;

    // Whether a gamepad was connected at the end of the previous tick, for the
    // rising-edge check in update().
    wasConnected = false;

    // True after update() has run in this drawn frame. render() sets it back to
    // false, so a frame that only draws leaves it false.
    updatedThisFrame = false;

    // Gamepad A, B, and Start presses that render() saw on a draw-only frame.
    // Each BT.BTN_* value is its own bit. The next update() performs them once.
    pendingGamepadEdges = 0;

    // Screen size, timing chart colors, and the keyboard scroll guard.
    configure() {
        return {
            displaySize: new Vector2i(DISPLAY_W, DISPLAY_H),

            // The default keyboard layout maps Space to the A button this demo reads -
            // keep the page from scrolling when it is pressed.
            isCapturingKeyboardScroll: true,

            isOverlayTimingChartEnabled: true,
            overlayTimingChartStyle: {
                updateBarPaletteIndex: C_CHART_DIM,
                renderBarPaletteIndex: C_POD_OUTLINE,
                tagPaletteIndex: C_CHART_TAG,
            },
        };
    }

    // Builds a small custom palette, installs the shared UI theme, and starts centered.
    async init() {
        // Build a small custom palette before any drawing happens. Think of each slot as
        // a numbered paint can the engine looks up while rendering.
        this.palette = BT.paletteCreate(256);

        this.palette.set(C_POD_OUTLINE, new Color32(245, 248, 255));
        this.palette.set(C_ARENA, new Color32(24, 30, 47));
        this.palette.set(C_ARENA_BORDER, new Color32(68, 80, 108));
        this.palette.set(C_CHART_DIM, new Color32(130, 144, 173));
        this.palette.set(C_CHART_TAG, new Color32(255, 190, 95));
        this.palette.set(C_POD_A, new Color32(120, 255, 170));
        this.palette.set(C_POD_B, new Color32(255, 130, 140));
        this.palette.set(C_POD_C, new Color32(120, 185, 255));
        this.palette.set(C_TRAIL, new Color32(255, 255, 255, 120));
        this.palette.set(C_AIM, new Color32(255, 220, 130));

        // The shared UI kit needs its theme colors in the palette before any ui.* call
        // can draw. applyTheme() writes them into high slots (240 and up), far away from
        // the scene slots above, and hands back a map like { bg: 240, text: 244, ... } so
        // this demo can reuse theme colors for its own drawing (we clear with bg).
        this.theme = applyTheme(this.palette);

        // Tell the engine to use this palette for every draw call from now on.
        BT.paletteSet(this.palette);

        // Place the pod and aim cursor in the middle of the arena.
        this.resetPod();

        return true;
    }

    // Reads keyboard edges, sticks, and triggers, and updates the toy state.
    // Gamepad button edges are read in render(), once per drawn frame.
    update() {
        // Let the UI kit do its once-per-tick housekeeping first. This demo has no kit
        // buttons or key bindings, but ui.tick() also tracks whether the screen has ever
        // been touched - that is what feeds the ui.hasTouch() hint drawn in render().
        ui.tick();

        // Ask the engine whether a gamepad is currently plugged in for this player slot.
        const connected = BT.isGamepadConnected(PLAYER);

        // "Edge detection": we only want to react the moment the gamepad is first
        // connected, not every single tick it stays connected. So we compare the current
        // state to what it was last tick (stored in wasConnected). If it just became true
        // (false -> true), that is the "rising edge" - the instant of connection.
        if (connected && !this.wasConnected) {
            // Label this moment on the overlay timing chart so you can see exactly which
            // frame the gamepad was detected.
            BT.assignTag('Gamepad connected');
        }

        // Save this tick's connection state so the next tick can compare against it.
        this.wasConnected = connected;

        // This frame did run update(), so render() can treat BT.isPressed as the
        // gamepad. Keyboard edges clear at the end of this method, so A, B, and
        // Start are read here, along with any gamepad press saved from a frame
        // that skipped update().
        this.updatedThisFrame = true;

        // A cycles the pod color once per physical press.
        if (this.consumeFacePress(BT.BTN_A)) {
            this.cyclePodColor();
        }

        // B toggles trail drawing.
        if (this.consumeFacePress(BT.BTN_B)) {
            this.toggleTrail();
        }

        // Start recenters the toy instantly.
        if (this.consumeFacePress(BT.BTN_START)) {
            this.resetPod();
        }

        // Axes are dead-zone filtered by the engine (see renderArena for the details).
        const moveX = BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_LEFT_X, PLAYER);
        const moveY = BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_LEFT_Y, PLAYER);
        const aimX = BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_RIGHT_X, PLAYER);
        const aimY = BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_RIGHT_Y, PLAYER);
        const throttle = Math.max(BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_TRIGGER_L, PLAYER), BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_TRIGGER_R, PLAYER));

        // Remember where the pod and aim cursor were before this tick moves them, so
        // render() can draw a smooth in-between position instead of a pop.
        this.prevPodPos = this.podPos;
        this.prevAimPos = this.aimPos;

        // Convert analog float values into integer pixel steps. While boosted, the pod
        // moves BOOST_FACTOR times faster; each tick uses one boost tick up.
        const speed = this.boostTicks > 0 ? POD_SPEED * BOOST_FACTOR : POD_SPEED;

        if (this.boostTicks > 0) {
            this.boostTicks -= 1;
        }

        this.podPos = this.podPos.add(new Vector2i(Math.round(moveX * speed), Math.round(moveY * speed)));
        this.aimPos = this.aimPos.add(new Vector2i(Math.round(aimX * AIM_SPEED), Math.round(aimY * AIM_SPEED)));

        // Keep both inside the arena. The pod's half size depends on the trigger pull,
        // the crosshair is always 4 pixels from center to tip.
        const podHalf = this.currentPodHalfSize(throttle);

        this.podPos = this.clampToArena(this.podPos, podHalf);
        this.aimPos = this.clampToArena(this.aimPos, 4);

        // With the trail on, remember this tick's position and drop the oldest point once
        // the list is full.
        if (this.trailEnabled) {
            this.trail.push(this.podPos);

            if (this.trail.length > TRAIL_MAX) {
                this.trail.shift();
            }
        }
    }

    // Draws the toy arena and the UI kit groups: title bar, hints, and the status panel.
    render() {
        // Gamepad edges for A, B, Start, and R2. The engine keeps a gamepad press
        // until the end of the drawn frame, then forgets it. render() runs once per
        // drawn frame, so each press is seen once: a fast screen can skip update()
        // for a frame, and a slow one can run update() twice. The Any Input demo
        // reads its gamepad helpers here for the same reason.
        //
        // After update(), the keyboard edge is already gone, so BT.isPressed is the
        // gamepad and the action runs now. On a frame that only draws, BT.isPressed
        // may still be a key update() has not read. That press is saved and performed
        // on the next update(), which is the only place this demo reads keys. R2 has
        // no key, so it always runs here. Sticks and the trigger pull that move the
        // pod stay in update(). Held state is safe in either method.
        if (this.noteGamepadPress(BT.BTN_A)) {
            this.cyclePodColor();
        }

        if (this.noteGamepadPress(BT.BTN_B)) {
            this.toggleTrail();
        }

        if (this.noteGamepadPress(BT.BTN_START)) {
            this.resetPod();
        }

        // R2, read as a button, fires once per pull past half way. The analog
        // pull that sets the pod's speed is still BT.getAxis in update().
        if (BT.isPressed(BT.BTN_R2, PLAYER)) {
            this.boostTicks = BOOST_TICKS;
        }

        // The next drawn frame has not run update() yet. A frame that only
        // draws leaves this false, which is how a saved press stays saved.
        this.updatedThisFrame = false;

        // Erase last frame with the shared theme background, then redraw from scratch.
        BT.clear(this.theme.bg);

        // The full-width title strip along the top edge.
        ui.begin(UI_ANCHORS.TOP_BAR);
        ui.panel('Gamepad Input - sticks, triggers, button masks');
        ui.end();

        this.renderHints();
        this.renderArena();
        this.renderStatusPanel();
        this.renderPodPanel();

        // When no gamepad is plugged in yet, show a friendly prompt inside the arena.
        if (!BT.isGamepadConnected(PLAYER)) {
            this.renderEmptyState();
        }
    }

    // True when a mapped keyboard key went down this tick (Space or B for A,
    // N for B, 5 for Start - the engine's own list, not a second copy), or
    // when render() saved a gamepad press of this button from a frame that
    // skipped update(). Keyboard edges clear at the end of update(), which is
    // why this runs there. One press runs the action once. The & test asks
    // whether that button's bit is set, and &= ~ clears it.
    consumeFacePress(button) {
        const fromKey = BT.DEFAULT_KEYBOARD_PLAYER1[button].some((key) => BT.isKeyPressed(key));
        const fromPad = (this.pendingGamepadEdges & button) !== 0;

        if (!fromKey && !fromPad) {
            return false;
        }

        this.pendingGamepadEdges &= ~button;

        return true;
    }

    // Reads this button's gamepad edge for render(). When update() already ran
    // this frame, returns true so the caller runs the action now. On a draw-only
    // frame, saves the press for update() and returns false. Does not read keys.
    noteGamepadPress(button) {
        if (!BT.isPressed(button, PLAYER)) {
            return false;
        }

        if (this.updatedThisFrame) {
            return true;
        }

        this.pendingGamepadEdges |= button;

        return false;
    }

    // Moves the pod to the next of its three colors, then back to the first.
    // The % operator gives the remainder, so the index wraps to 0.
    cyclePodColor() {
        this.podColorIndex = (this.podColorIndex + 1) % POD_COLOR_NAMES.length;
    }

    // Turns the breadcrumb trail on or off. Clearing the list when it goes off
    // keeps the trail from jumping across the arena the next time it is on.
    toggleTrail() {
        this.trailEnabled = !this.trailEnabled;

        if (!this.trailEnabled) {
            this.trail = [];
        }
    }

    // Returns the palette slot of the current pod color.
    currentPodColor() {
        if (this.podColorIndex === 0) {
            return C_POD_A;
        }

        if (this.podColorIndex === 1) {
            return C_POD_B;
        }

        return C_POD_C;
    }

    // Converts trigger pressure (0 to 1) into the pod's size in whole pixels.
    currentPodSize(throttle) {
        return POD_BASE_SIZE + Math.round(throttle * POD_MAX_EXTRA_SIZE);
    }

    // Returns half of the rendered pod size, rounded down to whole pixels.
    currentPodHalfSize(throttle) {
        return Math.floor(this.currentPodSize(throttle) / 2);
    }

    // Keeps a point inside the play area so that a square of the given `radius` around it
    // never pokes through the arena border. Returns the clamped position.
    clampToArena(pos, radius) {
        // The center may come no closer to a wall than its own radius, so the pod's edge
        // stops right at the arena border instead of poking through it.
        const minX = ARENA_X + radius;
        const maxX = ARENA_X + ARENA_W - 1 - radius;
        const minY = ARENA_Y + radius;
        const maxY = ARENA_Y + ARENA_H - 1 - radius;

        // Math.min picks the smaller of two numbers, Math.max the larger; chaining them
        // "clamps" a value so it can never leave the min..max range.
        const clampedX = Math.max(minX, Math.min(maxX, pos.x));
        const clampedY = Math.max(minY, Math.min(maxY, pos.y));

        return new Vector2i(clampedX, clampedY);
    }

    // Puts the pod in the arena center and the aim cursor 28 pixels to its right.
    resetPod() {
        this.podPos = new Vector2i(ARENA_X + Math.floor(ARENA_W / 2), ARENA_Y + Math.floor(ARENA_H / 2));
        this.aimPos = this.podPos.add(new Vector2i(28, 0));

        // Snap prevPodPos/prevAimPos to match, so render() does not blend in from
        // wherever the pod was before the reset (Start button press).
        this.prevPodPos = this.podPos;
        this.prevAimPos = this.aimPos;

        this.trail = [];
        this.boostTicks = 0;
    }

    // The Controls panel at the top of the left column: what each stick, trigger, and
    // button does, as four dim lines.
    renderHints() {
        ui.begin(UI_ANCHORS.TOP_LEFT, { x: EDGE, y: TOP_Y, width: LEFT_W });
        ui.panel('Controls');
        ui.label('L stick moves, R stick aims', { color: 'dim' });
        ui.label('Triggers grow the pod', { color: 'dim' });
        ui.label('A color, B trail, R2 boost', { color: 'dim' });
        ui.label('Start recenters', { color: 'dim' });
        ui.end();
    }

    // Draws the arena border, the optional trail, the pod, and the aim cursor.
    renderArena() {
        // Play area: a filled rectangle with a border so the pod has visible walls.
        BT.drawRectFill(new Rect2i(ARENA_X, ARENA_Y, ARENA_W, ARENA_H), C_ARENA);
        BT.drawRect(new Rect2i(ARENA_X, ARENA_Y, ARENA_W, ARENA_H), C_ARENA_BORDER);

        // Optional breadcrumb trail: one pixel per past pod position when B toggled it
        // on.
        if (this.trailEnabled) {
            for (let i = 0; i < this.trail.length; i++) {
                const p = this.trail[i];

                BT.drawPixel(p, C_TRAIL);
            }
        }

        // BT.getAxis returns a float from -1 to +1 for sticks, 0 to +1 for triggers. The
        // engine applies a "dead zone" first: a stick axis below 0.75 of full travel (the
        // default) reads as 0, and the rest is stretched back out to the full range, so
        // the pod does not drift when you let go of the stick. We read BOTH triggers and
        // keep whichever is squeezed harder (Math.max).
        const throttle = Math.max(BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_TRIGGER_L, PLAYER), BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_TRIGGER_R, PLAYER));
        const size = this.currentPodSize(throttle);
        const half = this.currentPodHalfSize(throttle);

        // Blend each entity's previous and current tick position by BT.renderAlpha so the
        // pod and aim cursor glide smoothly across render frames instead of snapping to a
        // new spot only once per tick (see the prevPodPos/prevAimPos comment above).
        const pod = Vector2i.lerp(this.prevPodPos, this.podPos, BT.renderAlpha);
        const aim = Vector2i.lerp(this.prevAimPos, this.aimPos, BT.renderAlpha);

        // Draw the pod as a square centered on its position; the white outline makes it
        // pop against the arena.
        BT.drawRectFill(new Rect2i(pod.x - half, pod.y - half, size, size), this.currentPodColor());
        BT.drawRect(new Rect2i(pod.x - half, pod.y - half, size, size), C_POD_OUTLINE);

        // Right-stick aim cursor: a small crosshair so both sticks have visible jobs.
        BT.drawLine(new Vector2i(aim.x - 4, aim.y), new Vector2i(aim.x + 4, aim.y), C_AIM);
        BT.drawLine(new Vector2i(aim.x, aim.y - 4), new Vector2i(aim.x, aim.y + 4), C_AIM);
    }

    // The right-hand status panel: connection info, live button pips, raw stick axis
    // numbers, and a trigger pressure meter. Everything read here is HELD state or an
    // axis value, both safe to read in render(). Button EDGES (BT.isPressed - "did it
    // go down just now?") are not read here: the gamepad half is at the top of
    // render(), and the keyboard half is in update().
    renderStatusPanel() {
        // Bitmask OR: BT.BTN_A | BT.BTN_B builds one mask. isDown returns true when
        // EITHER button is held - handy for "press any of these" checks in games. The two
        // single-button pips above it let you watch the OR happen live.
        const aHeld = BT.isDown(BT.BTN_A, PLAYER);
        const bHeld = BT.isDown(BT.BTN_B, PLAYER);
        const maskHeld = BT.isDown(BT.BTN_A | BT.BTN_B, PLAYER);

        // Raw axis values for the readout rows - the same calls the movement code uses.
        const moveX = BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_LEFT_X, PLAYER);
        const moveY = BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_LEFT_Y, PLAYER);
        const aimX = BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_RIGHT_X, PLAYER);
        const aimY = BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_RIGHT_Y, PLAYER);
        const throttle = Math.max(BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_TRIGGER_L, PLAYER), BT.getAxis(BT.AXIS_TRIGGER_R, PLAYER));

        // The panel title says how many gamepads the browser reports; the first pip says
        // whether player one has one.
        ui.begin(UI_ANCHORS.TOP_LEFT, { x: RIGHT_X, y: TOP_Y, width: RIGHT_W });
        ui.panel(`Gamepads: ${BT.gamepadCount}`);
        ui.pip('P1 connected', BT.isGamepadConnected(PLAYER));

        // Pips light up while a button is physically held down right now.
        ui.pip('A held', aHeld);
        ui.pip('B held', bHeld);
        ui.pip('(A|B) mask', maskHeld);

        // Lit while ANY gamepad button is held (D-pad, face, shoulders, Start, Select -
        // not sticks or triggers). BT.isAnyButtonPressed(player) is the matching edge for
        // "press any button".
        ui.pip('Any button', BT.isAnyButtonDown(PLAYER));

        // The triggers as DIGITAL buttons: held once pulled past half way. The Throttle
        // meter below shows the same triggers as an ANALOG 0 to 1 pull.
        ui.pip('L2 held', BT.isDown(BT.BTN_L2, PLAYER));
        ui.pip('R2 held', BT.isDown(BT.BTN_R2, PLAYER));

        // LX/LY are the left stick, RX/RY the right stick, each from -1.00 to +1.00.
        ui.kv('LX', formatAxis(moveX));
        ui.kv('LY', formatAxis(moveY));
        ui.kv('RX', formatAxis(aimX));
        ui.kv('RY', formatAxis(aimY));

        // The meter fills left-to-right with trigger pressure (0 = released, 1 = fully
        // squeezed) - the same value that grows the pod.
        ui.meter('Throttle', throttle, { width: METER_W });
        ui.end();
    }

    // The Pod panel under the status panel: what A, B, and R2 have done to the pod. These
    // work from the keyboard too (Space or B for A, N for B), so this panel reacts even
    // without a gamepad - except the boost, which needs R2.
    renderPodPanel() {
        ui.begin(UI_ANCHORS.TOP_LEFT, { x: RIGHT_X, y: POD_PANEL_Y, width: RIGHT_W });
        ui.panel('Pod');
        ui.kv('Color', POD_COLOR_NAMES[this.podColorIndex]);
        ui.kv('Trail', this.trailEnabled ? 'on' : 'off');

        // The boost meter is full the tick R2 starts a boost and empties as boostTicks
        // counts down to 0.
        ui.meter('Boost', this.boostTicks / BOOST_TICKS, { width: METER_W });
        ui.end();
    }

    // The "no gamepad yet" prompt, shown inside the empty arena as warm kit labels in a
    // borderless group. Pinned near the top of the arena so the idle pod and aim
    // crosshair (arena center) do not sit on the text.
    renderEmptyState() {
        ui.begin(UI_ANCHORS.TOP_LEFT, { x: ARENA_X + 6, y: ARENA_Y + 6 });

        // ui.hasTouch() turns true after the first touch contact and stays true. Touch
        // devices rarely have a gamepad attached, so tell those visitors plainly that
        // this page cannot work for them.
        if (ui.hasTouch()) {
            ui.label('This demo needs a gamepad.', { color: 'warm' });
        } else {
            ui.label('Connect a gamepad and press', { color: 'warm' });
            ui.label('any button to wake it.', { color: 'warm' });
        }

        ui.end();
    }
}

bootstrap(Demo);
```
